paper_metadata.title: Value of the Early Electroencephalogram After a First Unprovoked Seizure

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study provides a clear description of the target population, recruitment setting (Mannheim department), and specific inclusion/exclusion criteria. The sample is a prospective cohort of adults with a first unprovoked seizure, and baseline characteristics (age, sex, seizure type) are well-documented.

items.label: Source of target population
items.prompt: The source population or population of interest is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: Since 1991 we have been following a cohort of 157 adult patients, who were admitted to our department, in Mannheim, after a certain first unprovoked seizure.
items.reasoning: The authors specify the geographic location and the clinical nature of the cohort.

items.label: Method used to identify population
items.prompt: The sampling frame and recruitment are adequately described, including methods to identify the sample sufficient to limit potential bias (number and type used, e.g., referral patterns in health care)
items.evidence_snippet: The patients were older than 16 years, and the first EEG was obtained within 48hours ofthe first seizure (95% ofthe patients being seen within 24 hours).
items.reasoning: Recruitment is prospective and hospital-based with a clear temporal link to the index event.

items.evidence_snippet: Patients were excluded from the primary analysis, if they (I) had a history suspicious of previous epileptic seizures, (II) presented with absence ormyoclonic seizures as initial seizure type, (III) if the first seizure was acute symptomatic, (IV) if they had a malignant brain tumor orMAIDS encephalopathy.

risk_of_bias_assessment.label: Study Attrition Summary
risk_of_bias_assessment.prompt: Loss to follow-up (from baseline sample to study population analyzed) is not associated with key characteristics (i.e., the study data adequately represent the sample) sufficient to limit potential bias to the observed relationship between PF and outcome.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The EEG (prognostic factor) was measured using a standardized protocol (10-20 system) and interpreted by two experienced neurophysiologists using a pre-defined 5-category scale. The timing (within 48 hours) was strictly controlled.

items.label: Definition of the PF
items.prompt: A clear definition or description of 'PF' is provided (e.g., including dose, level, duration of exposure, and clear specification of the method of measurement).
items.evidence_snippet: All EEGs were recorded on 16-channel video-splitscreen instruments with both referential and bipolar recordings bymeans ofthe International 10-20 electrode placement System.
items.reasoning: The measurement technique and classification system (Table 1) are explicitly defined.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of PF
items.prompt: Method of PF measurement is adequately valid and reliable to limit misclassification bias (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and limited reliance on recall).
items.evidence_snippet: EEGs were rated by two experienced neurophysiologists (the authors) according to a fixed protocol.
items.reasoning: Use of a fixed protocol and experienced raters supports reliability.

items.prompt: Continuous variables are reported or appropriate cut-points (i.e., not data-dependent) are used.
items.evidence_snippet: The findings were classified in 5 categories (Table 1).
items.reasoning: The categories are standard clinical EEG classifications, not derived post-hoc from the data.

items.label: Method and Setting of PF Measurement
items.prompt: The method and setting of measurement of PF is the same for all study participants.
items.evidence_snippet: All EEGs were performed with hyperventilation for 3 minutes and intermittent photic stimulation.
items.reasoning: Standardized procedures were applied to all subjects.
